content.content: When invoked with `--to <id>` naming an id that maps to no node, the deccy CLI shall refuse the invocation, naming the id, and place nothing — creation stays the caller's. An id maps to no node when either the id names no change or the change it names carries no node document.
content.rationale: Attribution stays caller-placed by symmetry with required --on; the verb never guesses birth, so missing homes wait for their owners. The map is the whole reach: a node is the change its document is read from (S2-read nqktpzuu, S2-set ryzlzrkk), so resolution (M-node-resolve wynwwtur) over the load (M-node-load sxonuzmr) is what decides whether an id has a node at all — an id naming no change and a change carrying no node document both map to no node, and the root, which resolves yet names no node, does too. D21 (tsspuwzo) stays the unknown-id refusal, and record still never guesses birth (lypvkskv). Refusing, and naming the id, keeps an unplaceable invocation from passing as a placed one.
